intro.text: We are a holding company whose principal businesses are regulated utilities in California and Texas. Our businesses invest in and operate electric and gas utilities and other energy infrastructure that provide energy services to customers. Sempra was formed in 1998 through a business combination of Enova Corporation and Pacific Enterprises, the holding companies of our regulated public utilities in California: SDG&E, which began operations in 1881, and SoCalGas, which began operations in 1867. We have since expanded our regulated public utility presence into Texas through our 80.25% interest in Oncor and 50% interest in Sharyland Utilities. Sempra Infrastructure’s assets include investments in the U.S. and Mexico with a focus on LNG, energy networks and low carbon solutions.

check.text: Company-reported free cash flow is read for quarters only, so free cash flow is calculated: operating cash flow − capital expenditures (−$3.3B).

fcf_note.footer: No company-reported free cash flow (read for quarters only): free cash flow here is calculated by the formula.

checks.text: The revenue lines add up to revenue from contracts with customers ($11.8B); other revenues of $1.4B (not from contracts with customers, such as hedging results) make total revenues $13.2B, the income statement’s figure.
Pre-tax earnings minus tax did not equal net earnings in the filing (often discontinued operations or equity-method income); pre-tax is shown as net earnings plus tax.
The filing has no operating income figure: operating profit is shown equal to pre-tax earnings.

analysis: Revenue was $13.2B in FY2024, down 21% year over year. Natural Gas, Gathering, Transportation, Marketing and Processing was the largest line at 55% of revenue. Natural Gas, Gathering, Transportation, Marketing and Processing lost $2.4B year over year (down 25%), 67% of the total change.

Operating profit was $3.7B, a 28.2% margin (up 3.6 points year over year). Total costs fell 25% while revenue fell 21%. Net earnings were $2.9B, down 7% year over year. The effective tax rate was 5.9%.

Operating cash flow was $4.9B (down 21% year over year), 140% of net income including minority interests. Non-cash charges added back $2.4B of depreciation and amortization and $0.09B of share-based compensation. Working capital and other items used $1.1B. Capital expenditures of $8.2B exceeded it, leaving free cash flow of −$3.3B.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
